natural_body: Targeted 40% discounts boost acquisition but sharply damage retention.

first.rationale: Current situation shows activation down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion down 4% QoQ. Memory 31 and 86 both demonstrated that reducing onboarding friction—simplified signup fields and shortened onboarding flows—produced durable lifts in activation and completion. These are the most directly applicable to the current problem. Memory 91 on activation messaging also supports this vector. Promotional pricing (memory 73) is explicitly ruled out due to documented retention damage. Referral incentives (memory 57) work best with established customers, not for addressing current activation decline. Enterprise sales assist (memory 44) targets a different segment. Simplifying onboarding addresses both the 4% completion decline and likely contributes to the 6% activation decline without the customer acquisition cost or retention damage risks of discounting. Verification of memories 31 and 86 will confirm the magnitude and durability of onboarding simplification effects before committing to a standard-scale rollout.
